newsitem.title: UK: British driver jailed after road rage murder.
newsitem.headline: British driver jailed after road rage murder.

text.p: A London car dealer was jailed for life on Thursday for a "road rage" murder after a minor collision.
Lee Gardiner, 25, pursued the other vehicle in the accident across north London last May in his turbo-charged Renault 5.
After threatening the three black occupants with a snooker cue, Gardner arranged on his mobile telephone to pick up a gun, Southwark crown court in London was told.
Gardiner waited until the trio returned to their car, and then shot two of the men and chased the third on foot into a nearby park.

He told his victims "I've got something nice for you" before gunning them down. He shot the first one in the face, fracturing his jaw, and then pumped two bullets from a .22 pistol into the head of Ghanaian Benjamin Worae, killing him instantly.
Gardiner then turned to two terrified bystanders and said: "You don't know me. Me a bad boy. Me a gangster".

Judge Gerald Butler told Gardiner said it was a "chilling thought that you murdered one man and attempted to murder another man simply because they were in a car which had been in collision with yours".

Prosecution lawyer John Bevan told the court: "This case is a dramatic example of how a total loss of self-control by a car driver can cause him to behave in an uninhibited and, in this case, murderous way - road rage taken to its extreme."
